## lib-thehive-writeback (N8N-2.2)
**Trigger:** called by playbooks through Execute Workflow, waiting for the result.
**Inputs:** `{thehive_alert_id, wazuh_alert_id, config, context: {playbook, n8n_execution_id}, actions: [text], metrics: {mode, alert_id, source, fields, attack_run_id}}`.
**Actions taken:** first writes the C11 asox-metrics document through lib-metrics-upsert (On Error = continue: never parks, never blocks the comment) and adds its line to the actions (`metrics: ok | skipped (<why>) | failed (<class>)`); then comments on the TheHive alert: first line `[asox-n8n writeback] wazuh-alert-id=<id>`, then playbook, n8n execution id and the actions taken. Idempotent: if a comment by n8n@asox.local with that first line exists, nothing is written. Each TheHive call has lib-config's timeout and is retried on a connection error, timeout or 5xx, never on 4xx (N8N-6.2); a failed post is retried through a new comment listing, so a post that timed out but was written isn't written twice. Failures, or the last call failing, go to lib-error (parked, with the number of calls).
**Systems changed:** TheHive (one comment on the alert); Wazuh indexer (the alert's asox-metrics document).
**Approval:** not needed (no system changes outside TheHive).
**Owner:** n8n.
Successful executions are not saved (N8N-6.5): the calling playbook records the result; failed ones are kept.
